-- ============================================================================= -- DSL Mapper Addon -- standalone DSL-specific layer for Mudlet's OWN -- built-in Generic Mapper. Added 2026-08-29 -- see docs/MAPPER_REDESIGN.md -- for the full research/design history behind this file. -- -- WHAT THIS IS: everything DSL-specific about how MyDSL's mapper fork -- works (door-verb parsing, sector/terrain coloring, move-cost tracking, -- GMCP room-data handling, the searchRoom()/area-export bug ports, the -- safe-delete map-menu addition) -- with ZERO copy of Mudlet's own -- generic_mapper.xml script bundled inside it. This package assumes -- Mudlet's own Generic Mapper is already installed (it ships built into -- Mudlet itself and is enabled by default for most players) and layers -- on top of it entirely through public functions and events -- nothing -- in this file edits, replaces, or requires a modified copy of stock. -- -- WHAT THIS IS NOT: this is not DSL_Generic_Mapper.xml (MyDSL's own -- internal fork, used by the DSL2/MyDSL profiles themselves). That file -- is a separately-maintained, lightly-patched copy of stock kept for -- MyDSL's own use, including 2 small diagnostic/bugfix tweaks embedded -- inside stock's own local (non-reassignable) functions that genuinely -- can't be replicated here without editing stock source -- an accepted, -- documented, minor gap versus that fork, not an oversight. Do not -- install both DSL_Generic_Mapper.xml and this addon in the same -- profile at the same time -- they are alternatives, not complementary. -- -- DEPENDENCY CHECK: deferred a few seconds after load (not checked -- immediately -- at t=0 there's no way to tell "stock hasn't loaded yet" -- apart from "stock isn't installed at all"). If Mudlet's own Generic -- Mapper still doesn't appear to be present after that delay, says so -- clearly instead of failing silently or crashing into confusing errors -- later when a DSL-specific function gets called with no map.* to hook. -- =============================================================================
tempTimer(3, function() if not (map and map.configs and map.echo) then cecho("\n<red>[DSL Mapper Addon] <white>Mudlet's own Generic Mapper doesn't appear to be installed or loaded.\n") cecho("<red>[DSL Mapper Addon] <white>This addon needs it first -- Mudlet ships it built in for most games.\n") cecho("<red>[DSL Mapper Addon] <white>Open the Mapper (Ctrl+M or the compass icon) once to let Mudlet install it, then reload this addon.\n") end end)
------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- Install-welcome text and uninstall cleanup, added 2026-08-29 per -- Mudlet's own documented package best practices (wiki.mudlet.org's -- "Manual:Best Practices" -- confirmed via direct fetch, not assumed): -- "hook into the sysInstallPackage event to give some introductory text -- about the package they just installed" and "undo any UI changes on -- uninstall". sysInstallPackage fires (arg[1] = package name) only for -- a real package install, not every script reload -- confirmed directly -- in Host.cpp's installPackage(). removeMapEvent() is the real Lua -- function this file actually calls, for tearing down the addMapEvent -- registration below (wiki.mudlet.org/w/Manual:Lua_Functions#removeMapEvent, -- confirmed against TLuaInterpreterMapper.cpp directly). removeMapMenu() -- is a real sibling function (same file, tears down a submenu and its -- children) but this addon has no submenu to remove -- MyDSL_MapperMenu.lua -- is the one that would need it, not this file -- so it's not called here. ------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Must be a real global (not local) -- registerAnonymousEventHandler's -- second argument is looked up by name in _G, a local function here -- would never actually be found or called. function dslMapperAddonInstallUninstallHandler(event, packageName) if event == "sysInstallPackage" and packageName == "DSL_Mapper_Addon" then cecho("\n<green>[DSL Mapper Addon] <white>Installed. This adds DSL-specific mapping (door verbs, terrain, GMCP room data) plus a Safe Delete option to Mudlet's own map right-click menu.\n") cecho("<green>[DSL Mapper Addon] <white>Needs Mudlet's own Generic Mapper (open the Mapper once if you haven't) -- this addon doesn't include a copy of it.\n") elseif event == "sysUninstallPackage" and packageName == "DSL_Mapper_Addon" then if map and map.dsl and map.dsl.registeredEvents then for _, id in ipairs(map.dsl.registeredEvents) do pcall(killAnonymousEventHandler, id) end end if type(removeMapEvent) == "function" then pcall(removeMapEvent, "dslSafeDelete") end end end
registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysInstallPackage", "dslMapperAddonInstallUninstallHandler") registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysUninstallPackage", "dslMapperAddonInstallUninstallHandler")
------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- The DSL-specific mapper layer -- copied verbatim from the git-tracked, -- tested DSL_Generic_Mapper.xml (not re-derived; see that file's own -- test/ coverage for what's verified here), with one small addition: -- a call to installAddonOverrides() appended to the end of install()'s -- body (see that function, defined further down) so the bug-fix/update- -- disable overrides fire at the correct, safe point in the load -- sequence -- everything else below this point is unchanged. ------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ============================================================================ -- DSL Generic Mapper 0.2.2 Minimal Hardening Layer -- Conservative fork layer: Generic Mapper remains the room engine. -- This layer only adds DSL text patterns, GMCP assist, passive sector metadata, -- passive door-state feeding, and tiny debug/status helpers. -- ============================================================================ -- REAL BUG found 2026-08-30, via Steven's own report ("still not -- updating terrain") turning up an empty mapper_desync_log.txt despite -- the diagnostic logging added earlier the same day: `profilePath` was -- referenced (map.dsl.logDesync(), map.export_area(), map.import_area()) -- but never actually DEFINED anywhere in this file. DSL_Generic_Mapper.xml -- (the old full-fork this addon's logic was derived from) has its own -- `local profilePath = getMudletHomeDir()` -- but that's scoped to THAT -- file's own separate script chunk, invisible here; this addon is a -- genuinely standalone script with no shared Lua scope with stock. Every -- call using it was wrapped in a pcall that silently swallowed the -- resulting "attempt to concatenate a nil value" error -- so -- logDesync() has been silently failing to write ANYTHING since it was -- added, explaining why every diagnostic built earlier today came back -- empty regardless of what was actually happening in the mapper. (The -- existing test suite never caught this either: mudlet_mock.lua's own -- test harness stubs a fake global profilePath, which happens to paper -- over exactly this gap.) local profilePath = getMudletHomeDir()
map.dsl = map.dsl or {} map.dsl.version = "0.2.13" map.dsl.base = "Generic Mapper 2.1.8" map.dsl.gmcp = map.dsl.gmcp or {} map.dsl.line_buffer = map.dsl.line_buffer or {} map.dsl.last_command = map.dsl.last_command or nil -- Converted to FIFO queues 2026-07-19 (code review, correctness bug): -- these used to be single overwritable slots. map.speedwalk()'s zero-wait -- branch (speedwalk_wait=false, speedwalk_delay=0 -- both real, -- user-toggleable configs) sends every queued direction and auto-inserted -- door-clearing command in one tight loop with no delay between sends. -- captureCommand() fired once per send, so the single slot settled on the -- LAST command in the batch before any server reply returned -- every -- door-state line streaming back afterward (e.g. "It's already open." for -- an earlier door) got attributed to that same final direction instead of -- the one that actually produced it. A FIFO queue lets each door-state -- reply consume the command context in the same order the commands were -- actually sent, which is the one ordering guarantee a text MUD protocol -- does give us (the server processes and replies to input in order). map.dsl.door_command_queue = map.dsl.door_command_queue or {} map.dsl.move_command_queue = map.dsl.move_command_queue or {} local DSL_COMMAND_QUEUE_MAX = 10 map.dsl.last_terrain_text = map.dsl.last_terrain_text or nil map.dsl.last_door_line = map.dsl.last_door_line or nil map.dsl.last_room_apply = map.dsl.last_room_apply or nil
function map.dsl.echo(msg) cecho("\n<yellow>[DSL Generic Mapper] <reset> " .. tostring(msg) .. "\n") end
-- dsl_ud(rid, key, placeholder) -- real bug found via Steven's own -- "dslroom raw" output ("Room weight: 1 (source=, samples=, avg -- cost=0.0)"): getRoomUserData() returns an EMPTY STRING for an unset -- key, not nil -- so plain tostring(getRoomUserData(...)) silently -- displayed a blank instead of a clear "not set yet" placeholder. Every -- display line below reads room userdata through this helper instead of -- calling getRoomUserData()/tostring() directly, so this can't recur -- field-by-field. (Functional code elsewhere -- applyMoveCost(), -- onTerrainLine() -- was already unaffected: it compares against a -- specific non-empty string like "manual", or already explicitly checks -- for "" itself, so this was a display-only bug.) function map.dsl.dsl_ud(rid, key, placeholder) local v = getRoomUserData(rid, key) if v == nil or v == "" then return placeholder or "?" end return v end
function map.dsl.updateDisabled() map.update_waiting = nil if map.update_timer then killTimer(map.update_timer); map.update_timer = nil end map.dsl.echo("Updater is disabled in the DSL fork.") return false end
local dsl_long_dirs = { n = "north", e = "east", s = "south", w = "west", ne = "northeast", nw = "northwest", se = "southeast", sw = "southwest", u = "up", d = "down", north = "north", east = "east", south = "south", west = "west", northeast = "northeast", northwest = "northwest", southeast = "southeast", southwest = "southwest", up = "up", down = "down" } local dsl_short_dirs = { north = "n", east = "e", south = "s", west = "w", northeast = "ne", northwest = "nw", southeast = "se", southwest = "sw", up = "up", down = "down" } local dsl_door_status = { none = 0, open = 1, closed = 2, locked = 3 }
-- DSL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT / dsl_context_fresh() -- real bug found reviewing -- this fork before deployment: last_door_command/last_move_command both -- stored a timestamp (os.time()) that nothing ever checked, so a stale -- context from long before could get "replayed" against a much later, -- unrelated door-state message (e.g. a generic "Ok." in a different -- room). A door/move command is only trusted to explain a game response -- within this window. local DSL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT = 6
local function dsl_context_fresh(entry) return entry ~= nil and entry.time ~= nil and (os.time() - entry.time) <= DSL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT end
-- door_command_queue/move_command_queue helpers -- see the queue -- conversion comment near their declaration above for why these replaced -- the old single overwritable slots. local function dsl_push_command(queue, entry) table.insert(queue, entry) while #queue > DSL_COMMAND_QUEUE_MAX do table.remove(queue, 1) end end
-- Pops (and discards) entries until it finds one still within -- DSL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT, or the queue runs out. local function dsl_pop_fresh_command(queue) while #queue > 0 do local entry = table.remove(queue, 1) if dsl_context_fresh(entry) then return entry end end return nil end
-- DSL_DOOR_VERBS -- real bug found reviewing this fork before deployment: -- the original pattern here was `cmd:match("^(open|close|lock|unlock|pick)%s+(%a+)$")`, -- using `|` for alternation the way PCRE/regex would -- but Lua's own -- string.match() uses Lua patterns, which have NO alternation operator at -- all ("|" is just a literal pipe character). That pattern could never -- match ANY real command, so the entire door-verb capture below was dead -- code in the shipped 0.2.2 build -- every "open/close/lock/unlock/pick" -- command silently fell through to the bare-direction "move" check further -- down, meaning last_door_command could never actually be set. Checking -- each verb individually (they're hardcoded literals, safe to splice into -- a pattern) is the correct Lua equivalent. local DSL_DOOR_VERBS = { "open", "close", "lock", "unlock", "pick" }
local function dsl_dir_from_command(cmd) if not cmd then return nil end cmd = cmd:lower():trim() for _, verb in ipairs(DSL_DOOR_VERBS) do local target = cmd:match("^" .. verb .. "%s+(%a+)$") if target then -- DSL's own help ("Open object-or-direction") confirms open/close/ -- lock/unlock/pick are real, valid verbs against BOTH a room exit -- ("open west") and a plain object/container ("open backpack") -- -- the third return value tells the caller which one this was, so a -- non-direction target is never conflated with "no door command at -- all" (see captureCommand() below for why that distinction matters). local dir = dsl_long_dirs[target] return dir, verb, (dir == nil) end end local dir = dsl_long_dirs[cmd] if dir then return dir, "move" end return nil, nil, false end
function map.dsl.normalizeSector(value) if not value or value == "" then return "unknown" end value = tostring(value):lower():trim() local exact = { inside = "inside", city = "city", field = "field", fields = "field", forest = "forest", hills = "hills", hill = "hills", tundra = "tundra", swim = "swim", ocean = "ocean", underwater = "underwater", desert = "desert", mountain = "mountain", mountains = "mountain", underground = "underground", ice = "ice", icy = "ice", unknown = "unknown" } if exact[value] then return exact[value] end if value:find("indoors", 1, true) then return "inside" end if value:find("city", 1, true) then return "city" end if value:find("fields", 1, true) then return "field" end if value:find("forest", 1, true) then return "forest" end if value:find("hills", 1, true) then return "hills" end if value:find("tundra", 1, true) then return "tundra" end if value:find("heated desert", 1, true) or value:find("desert", 1, true) then return "desert" end if value:find("underground", 1, true) then return "underground" end if value:find("mountains", 1, true) then return "mountain" end if value:find("very icy", 1, true) then return "ice" end if value:find("undetermined", 1, true) then return "unknown" end -- Real gap found live 2026-07-18, per Steven ("is there a terrain -- color for air? its not adding it to the mapper") -- confirmed via -- his own log: DSL's real response to "terrain" while flying/airborne -- is "There is no terrain, your in the air!!!" -- a completely -- different message shape than every other terrain line (none of the -- others start with "There is no terrain"), so it never matched any -- existing pattern and was silently falling through to the -- catch-all "return value" below (an unrecognized, unnormalized -- string), never getting an environment color. if value:find("no terrain", 1, true) and value:find("in the air", 1, true) then return "air" end return value end
function map.dsl.captureCommand(cmd) if not cmd then return end cmd = tostring(cmd):lower():trim() map.dsl.last_command = cmd local dir, verb, nonDirectional = dsl_dir_from_command(cmd) if verb == "move" then dsl_push_command(map.dsl.move_command_queue, { raw = cmd, dir = dir, time = os.time() }) map.dsl.captureMovePoints() elseif verb and nonDirectional then -- Real bug found reviewing this fork before deployment: "open -- backpack"/"close pouch"/etc. are real door-verb commands aimed at -- a container, not a room exit. This used to fall into the branch -- below and store last_door_command with dir=nil -- then -- onDoorLine()'s fallback chain (`cmd and cmd.dir or move and -- move.dir`) would silently use the LAST MOVEMENT direction instead, -- misattributing a container's "It's already open." to whatever exit -- the player last walked through. Pushing a dir=nil marker onto BOTH -- queues (not just the door one) reserves this command's own place in -- the reply order with "no direction," so its eventual reply is -- correctly attributed to nothing -- a container action means any -- earlier movement is no longer what a new door-state message would -- be describing either, and this must not shift positions in the -- queue the way clearing/wiping it entirely would. dsl_push_command(map.dsl.door_command_queue, { raw = cmd, dir = nil, verb = verb, time = os.time() }) dsl_push_command(map.dsl.move_command_queue, { raw = cmd, dir = nil, time = os.time() }) elseif verb then dsl_push_command(map.dsl.door_command_queue, { raw = cmd, dir = dir, verb = verb, time = os.time() }) end end
local DSL_LINE_BUFFER_MAX = 80 local DSL_LINE_BUFFER_HIGH_WATER = 160
-- Batch-trims instead of shifting one line off the front every single call -- -- fixed 2026-07-19 after a PVP perf audit found this ran on EVERY line -- of ALL game output (registered on onNewLine, not scoped to moves), and -- table.remove(buf,1) is O(n): once the buffer hit its cap, every -- subsequent line paid for shifting ~80 elements down by one, and text -- volume is highest exactly during combat/PVP, not during movement. Now -- the buffer is allowed to grow to a high-water mark before trimming back -- down to the real cap in one pass, amortizing that cost across many -- lines instead of paying it on every single one. Still a plain -- 1-indexed array afterward, so extractVisibleRoomBlock()'s consumption -- of it is unaffected. function map.dsl.captureLine() if not line then return end local buf = map.dsl.line_buffer buf[#buf + 1] = tostring(line) local oldLen = #buf if oldLen > DSL_LINE_BUFFER_HIGH_WATER then local excess = oldLen - DSL_LINE_BUFFER_MAX for i = 1, DSL_LINE_BUFFER_MAX do buf[i] = buf[i + excess] end for i = DSL_LINE_BUFFER_MAX + 1, oldLen do buf[i] = nil end end end
local function dsl_join_exits_from_gmcp(exits) if type(exits) ~= "table" then return "" end local out = {} for _, d in ipairs(exits) do local s = tostring(d or ""):lower() out[#out + 1] = dsl_long_dirs[s] or s end return table.concat(out, " ") end
function map.dsl.extractVisibleRoomBlock(room_name) local buf = map.dsl.line_buffer or {} local exit_i for i = #buf, 1, -1 do if tostring(buf[i] or ""):match("^%s*%[Exits:%s*.*%]%s*$") then exit_i = i break end end if not exit_i and line and tostring(line):match("^%s*%[Exits:%s*.*%]%s*$") then exit_i = #buf + 1 end if not exit_i then return nil, nil end
local room_i local wanted = tostring(room_name or ""):trim() if wanted ~= "" then for i = exit_i - 1, 1, -1 do if tostring(buf[i] or ""):trim() == wanted then room_i = i break end end end
-- Fallback: choose the nearest nonblank line before the description block if GMCP name was unavailable. if not room_i then for i = exit_i - 1, 1, -1 do local candidate = tostring(buf[i] or ""):trim() if candidate ~= "" and not candidate:match("^%[") then room_i = i break end end end if not room_i then return nil, nil end
local desc = {} for i = room_i + 1, exit_i - 1 do local l = tostring(buf[i] or "") local t = l:trim() if t ~= "" and not t:match("^%[Exits:") then for _, pat in ipairs(map.save and map.save.ignore_patterns or {}) do t = string.trim(string.gsub(t, pat, "")) end if t ~= "" then desc[#desc + 1] = t end end end
local raw = {} for i = room_i, exit_i do raw[#raw + 1] = tostring(buf[i] or "") end if exit_i == #buf + 1 and line then raw[#raw + 1] = tostring(line) end return table.concat(desc, "\n"), table.concat(raw, "\n") end
-- How stale a GMCP room_data payload can be and still be trusted here -- -- fixed 2026-07-19 (code review): there was previously no sequencing check -- at all tying a given room_data payload to the specific visible-text -- block beforeExits() is processing right now. docs/DSL_CommandRef.md -- confirms char_data/room_data normally fire together on every prompt, so -- a genuinely current payload should be at most a fraction of a second -- old by the time the exits line triggers this function -- 2 seconds -- gives real margin for processing lag without being so long it could -- plausibly still be describing the PREVIOUS room. local DSL_GMCP_ROOMDATA_TIMEOUT = 2
-- roomLooksStale(rid) -- real bug reported by Steven: walking into a room -- Generic Mapper fails to resolve/create leaves map.currentRoom stuck on -- the PREVIOUS room, so a GMCP or "terrain" payload describing the room -- the player actually just entered gets filed onto that stale room's data -- instead (its color/terrain silently changes to match wherever the -- player really is, not what that mapped room actually is). rd.room is -- the same fresh-checked GMCP room name beforeExits() already trusts as -- ground truth to feed map.prompt.room, so comparing it against the -- candidate room's own stored name detects the desync directly instead of -- guessing from timing. Returns false (trust rid) whenever GMCP is -- missing/stale/nameless -- this must never be the reason a room fails to -- get colored on a normal move where GMCP just isn't fast enough yet. -- Real corpus check, 2026-08-24, in response to Claude Desktop's review of -- this function: does rd.room (GMCP) really agree with getRoomName()'s -- text-scraped name for the same real room, or could they format -- differently and false-positive this into blocking color on every such -- room? Checked all 260 log/ files with a GMCP dump: 89 of 98 rd.room -- values matched a standalone displayed header line in the same file -- exactly; the other 9 are fully explained, not real drift -- 8 are the -- literal string "darkness" (DSL's own GMCP placeholder for "too dark to -- see the room name," never a real room's actual name -- handled below) -- and 1 is a log file that started mid-visit, after the header had -- already printed in a previous session's log. Zero evidence of genuine -- GMCP-vs-display formatting drift for a real room name. function map.dsl.roomLooksStale(rid) local rd = map.dsl.gmcp and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data local rdFresh = rd and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time and (os.time() - map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time) <= DSL_GMCP_ROOMDATA_TIMEOUT if not rdFresh or not rd.room then return false end local gmcpName = tostring(rd.room):trim() -- "darkness" isn't a room name to compare -- treating it as an ordinary -- mismatch would still be safe (skip = no corruption) but would also -- needlessly block the sector/color write, since the corpus confirms -- rd.sector keeps reporting correctly even while the room name is dark. if gmcpName == "" or gmcpName:lower() == "darkness" then return false end local roomName = tostring(getRoomName(rid) or ""):trim() return roomName ~= "" and roomName ~= gmcpName end
-- Desync logger + checker -- added 2026-08-30 per Steven ("debug data -- first", then "do all recommended" once told this architecture can't -- reuse DSL_Generic_Mapper.xml's check_room()/move_map()/find_me()-level -- logging: those are stock-private locals here, unreachable from an -- addon layered on top through public functions and events only, per -- this file's own header. This is the addon-compatible equivalent, -- built entirely from what IS public: roomLooksStale() above already -- detects the exact symptom (map.currentRoom's stored name no longer -- matches where fresh GMCP says the player actually is) -- it was only -- ever used defensively before (block a color/terrain write onto the -- wrong room), never logged as a finding in its own right. Always-on, -- not gated behind "map config debug true" -- same reasoning as the -- other file: Steven shouldn't have to remember to flip that on before -- every session just so a rare desync gets caught when it happens. function map.dsl.logDesync(msg) local ok, f = pcall(io.open, profilePath .. "/mapper_desync_log.txt", "a") if ok and f then f:write(os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") .. " " .. tostring(msg) .. "\n") f:close() end end
-- Called on a short defer from onRoomData(), not inline -- GMCP and -- stock's own text-trigger-driven room resolution are two independent -- event streams reacting to the same server output, with no guaranteed -- ordering between them. Checking the instant GMCP arrives would flag a -- normal, fast, SUCCESSFUL move as a false-positive desync any time GMCP -- happens to win that race. A 1-second grace period gives stock's own -- resolution time to finish first; a genuine desync is not a timing -- fluke and is still just as visible a full second later. -- Widened 2026-08-30 (same day, Steven confirmed "the dot never moves at -- all" -- option 1 of 3) to log EVERY check, not just a mismatch. A -- silent "nothing logged" result was ambiguous between "no bug" and "the -- check never saw good data to compare in the first place" (e.g. GMCP -- room_data not actually refreshing, or map.currentRoom never set at -- all -- both previously silent early-returns here). Verbose on purpose -- while this is still an open investigation; narrow back to -- mismatch-only logging once the real cause is confirmed. function map.dsl.checkRoomDesync() local rd = map.dsl.gmcp and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data local gmcpName = rd and rd.room local rdAge = map.dsl.gmcp and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time and string.format("%.1fs", os.time() - map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time) or "never" if not map.currentRoom then map.dsl.logDesync(string.format( "no map.currentRoom set at all -- fresh GMCP says player is in %q (gmcp age %s)", tostring(gmcpName), rdAge)) return end if not map.roomexists or not map.roomexists(map.currentRoom) then map.dsl.logDesync(string.format( "map.currentRoom=%s does not exist in the loaded map database -- GMCP says player is in %q (gmcp age %s)", tostring(map.currentRoom), tostring(gmcpName), rdAge)) return end local storedName = getRoomName(map.currentRoom) local stale = map.dsl.roomLooksStale(map.currentRoom) map.dsl.logDesync(string.format( "check: currentRoom=%s stored_name=%q gmcp_name=%q gmcp_age=%s -> %s", tostring(map.currentRoom), tostring(storedName), tostring(gmcpName), rdAge, stale and "STUCK (mismatch)" or "ok")) end
function map.dsl.beforeExits(exits) map.prompt = map.prompt or {} exits = tostring(exits or ""):trim() local rd = map.dsl.gmcp and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data or {} local rdFresh = map.dsl.gmcp and map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time and (os.time() - map.dsl.gmcp.room_data_time) <= DSL_GMCP_ROOMDATA_TIMEOUT
-- GMCP assists Generic Mapper by filling prompt fields. It does not -- create rooms or links by itself. Only trust rd.room when it's fresh -- -- otherwise this is still holding a previous room's payload (GMCP hasn't -- sent a new one yet for this arrival), and falling through to the -- text-based capture below is safer than filing the new room's visible -- text under the old room's name. if rdFresh and rd.room and tostring(rd.room):trim() ~= "" then map.prompt.room = tostring(rd.room):trim() end if exits ~= "" then map.prompt.exits = exits elseif rdFresh and rd.exits then map.prompt.exits = dsl_join_exits_from_gmcp(rd.exits) end
local desc, raw = map.dsl.extractVisibleRoomBlock(map.prompt.room) if desc and desc ~= "" and map.configs and map.configs.use_description_matching then map.prompt.description = desc end if raw and raw ~= "" then map.dsl.last_raw_room_block = raw end map.dsl.last_visible_exits = map.prompt.exits end
-- Rewritten 2026-07-19 (code review, correctness bug): the previous version -- also re-searched the WHOLE queue by value for the failed direction and -- removed the first backward match, on the theory that a stale "look" -- entry (from search_on_look) could sit at position 1 and cause stock's -- own `table.remove(move_queue,1)` (map.eventHandler, registered earlier, -- always fires first on this same event) to remove the wrong thing, -- leaving the actual failed direction still queued somewhere else. -- Real bug: there is no way to tell "stock's removal was already correct" -- apart from "stock grabbed a stale look instead" from inside this -- function -- both look identical (a queue with no obvious problem). On a -- repeated-direction route (e.g. north,east,north where the first north -- fails), stock's removal is already correct, but the old code's blind -- value-search would then find and delete the SECOND, still-legitimate -- future "north", silently dropping a real queued step. Since -- search_on_look is now kept reliably off by install() (see the sticky -- fix above), "look" should never actually reach move_queue in the first -- place, so stock's own removal will always correctly target the failed -- move -- this function no longer needs to (unsoundly) second-guess it. -- What's left is defense-in-depth for a player who manually re-enables -- search_on_look: strip any stale "look" left stuck at the very FRONT of -- the queue. Restricting this to the front only (never a full scan) means -- it can never remove a genuinely future-queued direction, however many -- times that direction repeats later in the route. function map.dsl.onMoveFailCleanup() if type(move_queue) ~= "table" then return end while move_queue[1] == "look" do table.remove(move_queue, 1) end end
function map.dsl.onCharData() if not gmcp or not gmcp.char_data then return end map.dsl.gmcp.char_data = table.deepcopy and table.deepcopy(gmcp.char_data) or gmcp.char_data end

Mechanism: record the player's current -- move points the instant a real movement command is sent -- (sysDataSendRequest fires before the command reaches the server), then -- when the destination room resolves, read move points again and store -- the delta as this room's observed entry cost. Averaged across repeat -- visits (via dsl.move_cost_samples/dsl.move_cost_total room userdata) -- so a single visit landing on a natural regen tick doesn't permanently -- skew the room's weight. function map.dsl.captureMovePoints() if not (gmcp and gmcp.char_data) then return end local mv = tonumber(gmcp.char_data.move) if mv then map.dsl.pending_move_points = mv end end
function map.dsl.applyMoveCost(rid) if not rid or not map.roomexists or not map.roomexists(rid) then return end local before = map.dsl.pending_move_points map.dsl.pending_move_points = nil if not before then return end -- Read once, reused below for the compare-before-write at the end -- (was a second identical getRoomUserData call before 2026-07-19). local weightSource = getRoomUserData(rid, "dsl.weight_source") if weightSource == "manual" then return end if not (gmcp and gmcp.char_data) then return end local after = tonumber(gmcp.char_data.move) if not after then return end

" for room " .. tostring(rid) .. " (before=" .. tostring(before) .. " after=" .. tostring(after) .. ")", true) return end
local samples = tonumber(getRoomUserData(rid, "dsl.move_cost_samples")) or 0 local total = tonumber(getRoomUserData(rid, "dsl.move_cost_total")) or 0 samples = samples + 1 total = total + cost setRoomUserData(rid, "dsl.move_cost_samples", tostring(samples)) setRoomUserData(rid, "dsl.move_cost_total", tostring(total))
